threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that and not knowing the secret bus routes marks you as a newcomer.
Caught the 133 last night, and a guy was arguing with a drunk pigeon over a sandwich. The bird won, flew off with half the bun. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I spotted a kid selling lemonade on the corner, right next to a street artist painting a mural. That vibe is pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, there’s an old tram line that’s basically a rolling art gallery - every car is painted differently. You can’t find that in other cities.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during Civic Center’s random evacuations. Tourists are still baffled by smoke alarms downtown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 28 with a guy reciting Shakespeare to a half-asleep crowd. Only in San Francisco do you get free performances along with your ride.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. But it's the little bakeries and independent shops on Carrer de Fr 33 that really capture our spirit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their reluctance to order tapas; they always go for a full meal instead. Classic rookie mistake!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 26 bus is reliable. It’s a wild card, like betting on the weather here.
Saw a guy in a parka serenading a sleeping passenger with a ukulele on the 37. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw kids painting a mural on the side of the U-Bahn station while a group of elders argued about the best kebab spot nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a public park where people casually bring their own grill, set up for hours, and no one bats an eye. That’s just a Saturday here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid Civic Center BART during a meltdown. Tourists just stare at the chaos, confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 last night doing a magic trick with his phone—swiped left and right, then vanished it. Muni’s stage for real life magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think every plaza is for partying, but locals know it’s the kids' playgrounds that keep the real vibe alive, especially in the mornings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their constant phone usage at La Rambla, oblivious to the street musicians right beside them.
